_comment: Recorded, expiring Pod Security Admission exceptions, required by ADR-0710 D-1's PRESENCE HALF: every Namespace declared in the repository carries pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted, OR carries a record here. This shape is NOT ADR-0710 D-3's. D-3's exception keys on 'the cluster version that forced it', which is the right key for a mutating webhook and unfillable for a storage namespace -- no cluster version forces node-local path provisioning. These records therefore key on the CAPABILITY that forces the relaxation, per D-1's own field list: namespace, psa_level, forcing_capability, compensating_control, expiry, owner. DATA, not code: canonical-JSON governed, council-architecture owned, sited beside governance/capability-registry.json because governance/ is the ADR-0562 meta directory for policy-as-data. An entry here is a debt with a date, never a permanent grant: a namespace whose expiry passes without renewal or remediation is RED, and the registry is shrink-only in intent -- the exit for every row is deletion, not renewal.

authority.not_this_shape: ADR-0710 D-3 (mutating-webhook exceptions key on cluster version; scoped to the mutating side and deliberately not reused here)

census.predicate: Counted over files that DECLARE `kind: Namespace` and carry a pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce key on that Namespace. An earlier revision of this file recorded 18/9, which came from grepping the label string across all YAML rather than over Namespace-declaring files, and was not reproducible at the commit it named.
census.note: One namespace, kube-system, is EMITTED FROM RUST and declared in no YAML file; a manifest-only scan misses it entirely.

exceptions.forcing_capability: Node-local path provisioning. The local-path-provisioner helper Pod mounts a hostPath under the Talos-adapted node path, which `restricted` forbids outright. Talos mounts /opt read-only, so the provisioner is pinned under /var.
exceptions.compensating_control: Local and dev cells only; production cells use the region CSI driver instead. The namespace hosts exactly one provisioner workload and no tenant workload, so the hostPath grant is not reachable by tenant code.
exceptions.owner_basis: no OWNERS file covers infra/gitops/; owner assigned to the council that owns ADR-0710 pending the infra/ drain re-homing this manifest under iac/
exceptions.exit_condition: Production cells adopt the region CSI driver and the local-path provisioner is no longer deployed; the record is then deleted, not renewed.

exceptions.declared_in_note: EMITTED FROM RUST. No YAML declaration of this Namespace exists anywhere in the tree, so every manifest-only PSA scan reports a false green for it. This record is the only place it is accounted.
exceptions.forcing_capability: Cluster trusted computing base. kube-proxy runs with hostNetwork and NET_ADMIN to program node dataplane rules, and the bootstrap CNI DaemonSet requires host-namespace and host-device access. `restricted` forbids both.
exceptions.compensating_control: Control-plane components only; no tenant workload is scheduled into kube-system. Cilium replaces kube-proxy in the deployed posture, which narrows the surface but does not remove the bootstrap requirement.
exceptions.owner_basis: os/ is a registered meta directory (rung 1) in governance/capability-registry.json; no narrower OWNERS file covers the emitting module
exceptions.exit_condition: Upstream Kubernetes does not permit a restricted kube-system; this record is expected to be renewed rather than retired, and its expiry exists to force periodic re-justification, not eventual deletion.

exceptions.forcing_capability: Node-pinned CI workspace provisioning for the ARC runner fleet: the local-path-provisioner helper Pod mounts a hostPath at the declared nodePath, which `restricted` forbids.
exceptions.compensating_control: CI-cell workloads only, no tenant workload. The fleet it serves is already retired -- the ARC scale sets sit at maxRunners: 0 and merge CI is GitHub-hosted per ADR-0716 -- so the grant is dormant rather than active.
exceptions.owner_basis: ADR-0630, which introduced the ARC substrate, is archived; ownership falls to the council pending teardown
exceptions.exit_condition: DELETION, not renewal. This record exists only so the presence half is satisfiable while the ARC teardown lands. When infra/arc/ci-workspace-storage.yaml is deleted with its scale-set tombstones, this row goes with it. The short expiry is deliberate: it is the shortest in the registry because this namespace should outlive it by the least.

deferred_labelling._comment: Namespaces that are NOT exceptions and NOT yet labelled, because labelling them today would REFUSE their own workloads at admission. A PSA label is not free: enforce: restricted requires seccompProfile RuntimeDefault at pod or container level, and a namespace labelled before its workloads satisfy that stops being documentation and starts being an outage. These are tracked here so the gap is visible rather than silently unlabelled.

namespaces.blocker: Its Deployment delegates container securityContext to the shared helper `oya.securityContext.restrictedContainer` (oya/governance/iac/helm/_oya-helpers/templates/_helpers.tpl), which sets allowPrivilegeEscalation, readOnlyRootFilesystem, runAsNonRoot, runAsUser and capabilities.drop — but NOT seccompProfile. PSA restricted requires it.
namespaces.unblock: Add `seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}` to the shared helper, which is consumed by exactly this class of workload, then label both namespaces in the same change.

namespaces.blocker: Same shared helper, same missing seccompProfile.
namespaces.unblock: Same one-line helper fix; the two namespaces unblock together.

not_claimed: That any of these namespaces is currently deployed. Cluster readback is unavailable; every record describes declared desired state only.
That this registry is enforced. No gate reads it yet -- ADR-0710 D-1's exit criteria require one, and registering that gate is separate work.
That the census counts are stable. They were measured at one ref and move with the tree.
